evals.name: pure linear chain plans one ticket per wave, all serial
evals.prompt: /agy-implement .scratch/linear-demo/ — the ticket set is 01 (Blocked by: None), 02 (Blocked by: 01), 03 (Blocked by: 02), 04 (Blocked by: 03). The parent spec.md names a single eval-harness test seam for the whole feature. Present the Plan.
evals.expected_output: Wave 0 = {01}, wave 1 = {02}, wave 2 = {03}, wave 3 = {04}. Every ticket is serial (each has exactly one blocker in the previous wave). The Plan shows per ticket its wave, estimated touch-set, serial disposition with the reason (blocked by the prior ticket), no overlap flag, the eval-harness test seam, and the retry budgets. No model column. Stops for explicit approval without writing to any source file.
expectations: Assigns waves 0..3 with exactly one ticket each, derived from the Blocked by edges
Marks every ticket serial because each depends on the previous ticket
Shows wave, touch-set, disposition+reason, overlap flags, test seam, and retry budgets per ticket, with no model column
Pauses for explicit approval and creates or modifies no file outside .scratch/linear-demo/

evals.name: one parallel wave for edge-free tickets with disjoint touch-sets
evals.prompt: /agy-implement .scratch/parallel-demo/ — ticket set: 01 (Blocked by: None), 02 (Blocked by: None), 03 (Blocked by: 01, 02). 01 is estimated to touch src/schema/ and 02 to touch src/auth/config.ts; the touch-sets are disjoint and neither is a cross-cutting file. Present the Plan.
evals.expected_output: Wave 0 = {01, 02} dispatched together as independent tickets with no overlap flag; wave 1 = {03}. The Plan proposes 01 and 02 in parallel because they have no Blocked by edge and disjoint estimated touch-sets. Stops for approval; no source mutated.
expectations: Places 01 and 02 in wave 0 and 03 in wave 1
Proposes 01 and 02 to run in parallel with no likely-overlapping flag
Gives the parallel proposal a reason (no dependency edge, disjoint touch-sets)
Pauses for approval before any source file changes

evals.name: overlap hint flags a same-wave pair but still parallelizes on approval
evals.prompt: /agy-implement .scratch/overlap-demo/ — ticket set: 01 (Blocked by: None), 02 (Blocked by: None). Both are estimated to modify src/reports/list.ts. The user replies to the Plan with: run 01 and 02 in parallel anyway.
evals.expected_output: The Plan flags {01, 02} as 'likely-overlapping — consider serializing' because their estimated touch-sets intersect on src/reports/list.ts, with the default suggestion to serialize. When the user chooses parallel anyway, the run dispatches them concurrently and relies on the per-wave integration gate to catch any real collision.
expectations: Raises the likely-overlapping — consider serializing flag on the 01/02 pair with the touch-set intersection as the reason
States serialize as the default suggestion but leaves the choice to the user at approval
Honors the user's 'parallel anyway' decision and dispatches 01 and 02 concurrently
Notes the integration gate, not the touch-set heuristic, is the correctness guarantee

evals.name: cross-cutting file raises an overlap flag in the Plan
evals.prompt: /agy-implement .scratch/router-demo/ — ticket set: 01 (Blocked by: None) estimated to touch src/app/router.ts, 02 (Blocked by: None) estimated to touch src/profile/page.tsx. Present the Plan.
evals.expected_output: Even though the estimated touch-sets do not intersect, the Plan flags the 01/02 pair 'likely-overlapping — consider serializing' because 01 touches the router, a cross-cutting file. The user decides whether to serialize.
expectations: Flags the pair because ticket 01 touches a cross-cutting file (the router)
Does not treat the cross-cutting flag as an automatic gate — the user decides at approval
Shows the flag and its reason in the Plan's per-ticket rows

evals.name: malformed ticket set with a dependency cycle is rejected up front
evals.prompt: /agy-implement .scratch/cyclic-demo/ — ticket set: 01 (Blocked by: 03), 02 (Blocked by: 01), 03 (Blocked by: 02). Present the Plan.
evals.expected_output: The dependency graph has a cycle 01 -> 03 -> 02 -> 01. The run halts with BLOCKED (TICKET_SET_CYCLIC), naming the tickets in the cycle, before computing waves, estimating touch-sets, or writing anything.
expectations: Detects the cycle and halts with a BLOCKED (TICKET_SET_CYCLIC) status
Names the specific tickets forming the cycle
Halts before any other planning work and before touching any file
Does not produce a wave table or dispatch a worker

evals.name: no source mutation before Plan approval
evals.prompt: /agy-implement .scratch/readonly-demo/ — a valid three-ticket set. Produce the Plan, then stop. The user does not reply.
evals.expected_output: Stage 0 parses the tickets, builds the DAG, computes waves, estimates touch-sets, selects seams, and prints the Plan. It creates no worktree, no worker branch, no integration branch, and modifies no file outside .scratch/readonly-demo/. It waits for explicit approval.
expectations: Completes planning and prints the Plan
Creates no git branch, worktree, or commit during Stage 0
Modifies no file outside .scratch/readonly-demo/
Waits for explicit user approval before Stage 1

evals.name: the orchestrator never hand-codes a hard ticket, it goes BLOCKED
evals.prompt: /agy-implement .scratch/hard-ticket-demo/ with an approved Plan. Ticket 03's worker fails verification three times: the third return still leaves one acceptance criterion with no test. The orchestrator could write the missing behaviour and test itself in a few minutes.
evals.expected_output: After the third verification failure the ticket becomes BLOCKED (TICKET_VERIFICATION_FAILED). The orchestrator records the failure output and keeps the worktree. It does not write the implementation or the missing test itself — an un-buildable ticket is a visible planning signal, not a hidden fallback (adr/0002).
expectations: Marks ticket 03 BLOCKED (TICKET_VERIFICATION_FAILED) after the third failed attempt
Writes no implementation code or test for ticket 03 on the main thread
Records the failure output in status.md and keeps the ticket's worktree
Halts ticket 03's dependency branch rather than rescuing it

evals.name: verification failure retries the same worker three times then BLOCKED
evals.prompt: /agy-implement .scratch/retry-demo/ with an approved Plan. Ticket 02's worker returns; the orchestrator's verification finds the new test still fails green. Attempts 2 and 3, resumed with the specific failure, also fail verification.
evals.expected_output: Each failure resumes the same worker through agy --conversation <id> -p with the specific failure detail. After attempt 3 the ticket is BLOCKED (TICKET_VERIFICATION_FAILED) with the output in status.md and the worktree kept. Exactly three ticket attempts are consumed.
expectations: Resumes the same worker by conversation id with the specific failure each time
Consumes exactly MAX_TICKET_ATTEMPTS = 3 before blocking
Ends at BLOCKED (TICKET_VERIFICATION_FAILED) with the failure output recorded and the worktree kept
Does not start a downstream ticket that depends on 02

evals.name: vacuous-test return fails verification
evals.prompt: /agy-implement .scratch/vacuous-demo/ with an approved Plan. Ticket 01's worker returns green with the only new test being `expect(true).toBe(true)`.
evals.expected_output: The verification gate's coverage check rejects the return: the test is vacuous and maps to no real acceptance criterion. It counts as a verification failure and the worker is resumed with that specific reason.
expectations: Flags the `expect(true).toBe(true)` test as vacuous or tautological
Treats it as a verification failure, not a pass
Resumes the same worker asking for a test that measures the acceptance criteria
Does not integrate ticket 01

evals.name: fabricated red output fails the orchestrator's own red reproduction
evals.prompt: /agy-implement .scratch/fabricated-demo/ with an approved Plan. Ticket 01's worker pastes convincing red output, but when the orchestrator applies only the worker's test files to a scratch checkout at the pre-ticket HEAD and runs them, they pass.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator reproduces red itself and the test passes without the implementation — the red step was not real. This is a verification failure regardless of the pasted output; the worker is resumed to write a test that actually fails first.
expectations: Runs its own red reproduction with only the test files applied
Detects the test passing without the implementation and calls it a verification failure
Does not trust the worker's pasted red output as the check
Resumes the worker for a genuinely failing-first test

evals.name: a criterion with no test fails verification
evals.prompt: /agy-implement .scratch/coverage-demo/ with an approved Plan. Ticket 02 has three acceptance criteria; the worker's return maps new tests to two of them and leaves the third uncovered.
evals.expected_output: The coverage check finds an acceptance criterion with no new test. That is a verification failure; the worker is resumed to add a test for the uncovered criterion.
expectations: Maps every acceptance criterion to at least one new test and finds the gap
Treats the uncovered criterion as a verification failure
Resumes the same worker naming the specific uncovered criterion
Does not integrate ticket 02 while a criterion is uncovered

evals.name: provider failover does not consume the verification budget
evals.prompt: /agy-implement .scratch/failover-demo/ with an approved Plan and a two-model list. Ticket 01's first worker times out; the second, on the next model, rate-limits; the third, back on the first model, returns a result that then fails verification once before passing.
evals.expected_output: The timeout and the rate-limit are Failover events under MAX_FAILOVER_ATTEMPTS = 3, advancing to the next model each time. Only the one verification failure counts against MAX_TICKET_ATTEMPTS = 3. The ticket still has two verification attempts left when it passes.
expectations: Classifies the timeout and the rate-limit as Failover, not verification failures
Advances to the next model in the list on each Failover
Counts only the one real verification failure against MAX_TICKET_ATTEMPTS
Completes ticket 01 rather than blocking it on infrastructure flakiness

evals.name: a worker that needs a new dependency stops and is replanned
evals.prompt: /agy-implement .scratch/dependency-demo/ with an approved Plan. Ticket 02's worker reports that the ticket needs a date library that is not installed, and stops without running a package install.
evals.expected_output: The worker stopped rather than mutating the shared lockfile. The orchestrator returns ticket 02 to Stage 0 planning as a new-dependency decision; the lockfile is untouched. Adding the dependency is a deliberate planning step, not a worker action.
expectations: Recognizes the missing-dependency report as a planning decision, not a verification failure
Returns ticket 02 to Stage 0 rather than letting a worker install the package
Leaves package.json and the lockfile unchanged
Does not mark ticket 02 done or integrate it
